item.title: Iran said it intercepted US MQ-1 Predator drone over Qeshm Island
item.description:
Iran said it intercepted US MQ-1 Predator drone over Qeshm Island

Iran said it had intercepted and destroyed a US MQ-1 Predator drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. 

In a statement to state media, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said its Aerospace Force downed the drone by using a "new advanced air defence system".

 The IRGC said the aircraft it downed was a failed "enemy reconnaissance mission" by the "aggressor US army".

item.title: Oil tanker on fire in Strait of Hormuz: Iran's navy
item.description:
Oil tanker on fire in Strait of Hormuz: Iran's navy

Iran’s navy said a second oil tanker caught fire on Saturday morning after hitting a naval mine while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz, according to state media.

“Fire and explosions are the fate of tankers involved in illegal activities that have turned off their tracking systems and are operating in restricted areas,” the navy said, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency.

The navy did not identify the vessel. It was the fifth oil tanker in 24 hours to catch fire after reportedly being struck by Iranian forces or hitting a naval mine while attempting to transit the strait.

item.title: Houthis say Saudi-led coalition forces target Saada, Razih in Yemen
item.description:
Houthis say Saudi-led coalition forces target Saada, Razih in Yemen

Saudi-led coalition air strikes targeted southern parts of Saada city in northern Yemen, while artillery shelling hit populated villages in the border district of Razih, Al Jazeera reported, citing Houthi-run Al Masirah TV.

Yemen’s government military spokesperson, Colonel Majed Al-Nuzaili, said on Friday that government forces carried out 943 strikes and targeting operations against Houthi positions as part of Operation Dawn of Yemen.

item.title: Morning update
item.description:
Morning update

Good Morning Middle East Eye readers,

If you are just joining us, here are key developments from across the region and beyond:

*US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said that further US military action against Iran is unnecessary because the economic pain the Washington is inflicting on a "weakened" Tehran "is so great".

*Iran's navy and Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday that fires had broken out on a total of three oil tankers that struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

*US President Donald Trump will discuss the Iran war with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week but he is not expected to discuss Ukraine war.

*As many as 25 seafarers have been killed in 134 confirmed maritime incidents across the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Middle East since the US and Israeli started war on Iran in February, according to the UN.

*A Palestinian youngster was injured after Israeli military forced its way into the town of Jaba', south of Jenin in the occupied West Bank, and fired live ammunition and tear gas canisters at  residents, Wafa reported.

*The US Central Command (Centcom) said its forces shot down two one-way attack drones launched by the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) towards Bahrain.

*At least seven tankers were attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz in the week to 11 November, UKMTO said, with one strike leaving multiple crew injured in the Arabian Gulf.

*US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has targeted the International Criminal Court (ICC) in a speech to a conservative legal group on Friday, arguing for a muscular foreign policy and against international law restraining US actions.

*The UN and its humanitarian partners have called on Israel to lift restrictions on aid deliveries to Gaza, warning that deadly rainstorms have killed children and adults, destroyed shelters and flooded thousands of family tents.

*Roman Gofman, chief of Israeli spy agency Mossad and one of Benjamin Netanyahu's closest confidants, was in Washington on Friday for talks with senior Trump administration officials about the war in Iran, Axios reported.

item.title: Iran says it targeted US military radar in Bahrain in retaliatory strike
item.description:
First direct attack on US military installations for months was in response to US airstrike on communications tower

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it has targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik overlooking the strait of Hormuz. It is Iran’s first direct attack on US military installations for months.

“This is a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end its aerial mischief and oil smuggling in the strait of Hormuz,” the IRGC said. “In the event of repeated violations and aggression, the IRGC aerospace force is on full alert to confront the enemy without constraint.”

item.title: Boxer on death row in Iran vows ‘not to bow before oppression’ after winning rights prize
item.description:
Political prisoner Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran, given prestigious Magnitsky humanitarian award

A boxer and political prisoner on death row in Iran said he will “never surrender” as he accepted a prestigious human rights prize on behalf of “the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives”.

Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, an Iranian boxing champion, coach and political prisoner, has been sentenced to death three times and is one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran. He was given the Magnitsky award for outstanding human rights activist at a ceremony in London on Thursday night.
